messages:
jon: proposing a small additive schema change for console telemetry: add compute_tier (hot|standard|cold) and per-tenant retention_days on route_metrics so we can tier storage and show retention in UI.

maria: high level ok. why not stick to labels/envelope?

jon: labels are inconsistent for query planners. explicit column simplifies partitioning and billing.

tara: migration concern — billions of rows. we can't rewrite the table.

jon: plan: ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN compute_tier TEXT NULL, ADD COLUMN retention_days INT NULL. Start with NULLs -> fallback to global defaults. Then run throttled, idempotent backfill updating NULLs in batches. No table rewrite.

kevin: queries might change plans when new columns exist.

jon: short term: no partition change. We'll create an MV aggregated by (route_id, day, compute_tier) to stabilize dashboard reads. Longer term: switch archive partitions to month+compute_tier.

maria: paste DDL and backfill sketch plz. also need safety checklist.

jon: DDL sketch:
ALTER TABLE route_metrics ADD COLUMN compute_tier TEXT NULL;
ALTER TABLE route_metrics ADD COLUMN retention_days INT NULL;
-- backfill (throttled): UPDATE route_metrics SET compute_tier='standard', retention_days=30 WHERE compute_tier IS NULL LIMIT 50000;
Backfill runs as a background worker with auto-throttle on p99 write latency.

tara: downstream consumers reading telemetry from Kafka? joins could break.

jon: new events will get compute_tier at enrichment. For downstreams that want it we emit a compatibility topic; old consumers unchanged. Historical rows only in storage.

kevin: mixed old/new rows risk double-counting in analytics.

jon: MV will dedupe by route_metric_id, prefer rows with retention_days set, and use updated_at to select latest. Aggregations read MV.

maria: backup/restore risk if rolling back to older schema?

jon: deploy phases: 1) add columns (app tolerant) 2) enrichment writes compute_tier for new events (dualwrite safe) 3) backfill 4) switch dashboards to MV 5) introduce partitioning/archive. App handles missing columns at each phase.

tara: who owns the backfill windows and throttling SLAs?

jon: eng-platform owns orchestration and per-tenant quotas; eng-infra manages DB windows. SLA: 10k updates/sec max, pause if db p99 write latency > 250ms.

kevin: monitoring & alerts?

jon: metrics: rows_updated_total, rows_updated_per_tenant, backfill_eta_seconds, rows_failed_total. Dashboard tile for percent migrated per tenant. Alert if any tenant ETA > 48h and tenant size >1TB. Also alert if failure rate > 0.1% per tenant.

maria: archive format?

jon: archive to S3 Parquet partitioned by month and compute_tier. Keep metadata index with tenant/month/compute_tier -> s3 path. Archived months not served in interactive console; retrieval async.

kevin: canary?

jon: yes — 5 tenants (small+mid), 48h canary. Validate MV parity vs legacy queries, billing delta <0.1%. If OK, stage cohorts.

ingest-bot: scheduled job created: compute-tier-backfill start=3301120000 throttle=10000rps owner=eng-platform

maria: add a short note for auditors describing retention_days semantics and edgecases with old backups.

tara: once runbook lands i'll review and sign off. :thumbsup:
